feature: A band swept inside a screen picks what is on that screen
summary: Dragging across a screen's empty background now draws a selection band that picks up the things on that screen, instead of picking the screen up and moving it. Screens still move: by a drag once they are picked, and by their name at any time.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default.

try.do: Press F, then drag out a screen on an empty canvas.
Press R and draw two rectangles inside it, well apart.
Press V, then click bare canvas outside the screen so nothing is picked.
Drag from an empty corner of the screen across both rectangles. A band appears, the screen's edge lights up, and both rectangles come out picked.
Click that same empty corner: the screen itself is picked, exactly as before.
Drag from the middle of the now-picked screen: it moves.
Press Escape, then rest the pointer on the screen's name and drag it: the screen moves without being picked first.

evaluate: When you drag on a screen's background, is a band what you expected, or did you mean to move the screen?
Does the lit screen edge read as the wall of the room you are picking in, or as one more thing the band has caught?
Is the name above a screen an obvious enough handle that you would reach for it to move the screen?
Having clicked a screen and picked it, does the next drag moving it feel right, or does it get in your way when you wanted to keep banding?
Should a band be allowed to catch things that only partly fit, or is fully-inside still the right rule on a screen?
rough: Same gesture, two meanings, decided by whether the screen is picked: dragging a screen's background sweeps when it is not picked and moves it when it is. That is Figma's rule and it is what stops a selected screen feeling stuck, but there is a real accident in it. Click a screen to look at its settings, then try to band its buttons, and you move the screen instead. One undo puts it back. Escape first is the way round it.

Nothing on screen tells the two apart before you press. The pointer stays an arrow either way. A cue on hover over a picked screen's surface would say it, and I left that out rather than invent a cursor for it in this task.
Option-dragging a screen's background used to duplicate the screen and now sweeps instead. Option-dragging its name duplicates it, so the gesture moved rather than went away, but nobody is told that.

The mock said nothing about how a screen moves once its surface is busy. I took Figma's answer (name label as the handle) and added the already-picked case on top, because a screen whose name has scrolled off the top of the window would otherwise have no drag at all.

Verified live: the probe held the Screen Recording grant, so both pictures here are real screen captures of the window, taken mid-gesture by the playtest Scripts/playtest/band-inside-a-screen-walk.json.
